coverage: overnight since the evening brief (~19:30); X Following back to about 20:00
headline: PHP2Shell was hit four days before the fix and now sees millions of attempts; GitLab and Railway add to the security night; Anthropic launches Claude Duet; US pulls staff from Saudi Arabia.

stories.title: PHP2Shell was being exploited four days before the fix, and attacks are now in the millions
facts: AWS says its MadPot honeypots logged a PHP2Shell exploit attempt on 17 October, four days before the embargo lifted, from an IP tied to a commercial anonymization network.
More attempts from several different anonymized sources hit AWS sensors between 04:00 and 10:00 Berlin on Wednesday, hours before the 16:00 release; AWS now calls it "broadly exploited in the wild".
AWS's advice: investigate from at least 17 October, not the disclosure date, and measure patch times for internet-facing systems in hours.
Cloudflare's Matthew Prince: thousands of attempts in the 10 hours before the announcement, tens of thousands in the 45 minutes after, and millions now.
Japan's Finance and Health ministries took parts of their websites offline to patch; the government says no damage has been reported.
Taylor Otwell says the Laravel team patched its products through the night and expects other languages to go through the same thing as agents get better at finding bugs.
stories.whyItMatters: Anyone who patched on Wednesday evening should still check logs from the 17th onwards: the embargo didn't stop everyone, and a patch is no proof nobody got in first.

stories.title: Same night: a CVSS 10 GitLab hole spanning 12 years, and Railway says customer secrets may have leaked
facts: GitLab shipped critical patches 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9, 19.1.9, 19.0.10 and 18.11.13 and says every self-managed install should upgrade immediately; GitLab.com is already patched.
The flaw, CVE-2026-110264, is rated CVSS 10.0 and lets an attacker run code without logging in; affected versions go back to GitLab 7.0.
Railway detected unusual activity on systems that store customer environment variables; an attacker may have read encrypted variables and, for some, the decrypted values.

Railway believes it's part of a wave of attacks on platform companies aimed at stealing AI inference keys, has asked upstream providers to revoke keys, and tells all users to rotate their variables now.
Vercel says firewall rules for the separate Node.js Brotli RCE were live before the official patch; Bun says v1.4.4 carries its fix.
stories.whyItMatters: If you self-host GitLab or keep secrets in Railway, this is a today job: upgrade, then rotate API keys and database credentials.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, a proactive agent that works while you're away
facts: Claude Duet is a research preview, by waitlist, for US Pro and Max subscribers; Team and Enterprise come later.
It's a separate app on iOS and Android plus claude.ai, and carries over your memory, skills and connected apps from Claude.
It runs on Claude Opus 5.5 in a virtual machine with its own browser, so it keeps working when your laptop or phone is off.
It checks your connected accounts every few hours, sends a morning brief, and asks before sending messages, paying, signing or deleting anything.
No extra charge in the preview, but its background checks count against your plan's usage limits; trading securities and moving money are off-limits.
The press frames it as Anthropic's answer to Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots.

stories.title: US pulls staff from Saudi Arabia after a deadly airport strike; NYT says new Iran strikes are planned for after the midterms
facts: The State Department ordered non-emergency staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing escalating attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis; it says the order covers Saudi Arabia only.
An attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one person and injured eight; earlier, a drone attack near Aramco's Shaybah oilfield killed two.
Reuters cites US officials saying family members will also be withdrawn from other missions in the region.
The New York Times reports US and Israeli militaries have drawn up plans for a "short but intensive" round of strikes on Iran after the 3 November midterms.
CNBC says Brent crude topped $110 a barrel on the escalation.

stories.title: Tesla beats on EPS and cash flow, but profit falls 43% as AI and Optimus spending climbs
facts: Q3 revenue $28.05bn, flat on the year; non-GAAP EPS $0.48 beat estimates, GAAP net income fell 43% to $787m.
Operating income fell 56% to $718m (2.6% margin) as R&D jumped 69% to $2.76bn.
Free cash flow was $1.53bn, and full-year capex guidance was cut to $20bn from $25bn.
Optimus production started at Fremont; Musk says reaching 20,000 robots a week will take at least a year.
Tesla's new Robotaxi safety report claims 3.3 million autonomous miles with zero injuries or airbag deployments.
Shares rose about 2% after hours, then reversed to trade 2–3% lower.

stories.title: Meta: a $25bn New Mexico penalty, a new non-voting share class, and capex up to $145bn
facts: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25bn in the Cambridge Analytica-linked privacy case; the state had been awarded $219.5bn before the cut.
The jury had found more than 43 million violations of the state's unfair practices act, each carrying up to $5,000.
Q3 costs include a $9.89bn charge for the teen-harm settlement with 52 attorneys general.
Meta narrowed 2026 capex to $135–145bn and guides Q4 revenue to $73–76bn.
WSJ: Meta will split its stock by creating a new share class to fund AI spending.

stories.title: Hours after both sides back three-way talks, Kyiv and Moscow trade heavy strikes
facts: Zelensky says Ukraine backs a US proposal for three-way talks at negotiator level as soon as possible; the Kremlin says Putin agreed in principle to resume after 10 November.
Missiles hit Kyiv early Thursday, wounding at least 15 and damaging subway infrastructure on the Southern Bridge.
Moscow's mayor says 630 drones were sent towards the region overnight, 163 of them at the capital.
A strike killed a woman in the Kharkiv region, and a drone hit energy infrastructure near Kremenchuk.

stories.title: EQT bids €46.50 a share for Qiagen, about €9.6bn
facts: EQT Private Equity is offering €46.50 per Qiagen share in cash, about €9.6bn for the equity and roughly €10.8bn including debt.
Qiagen's boards recommend the voluntary offer; ADIA and CPP Investments are co-investors.
Conditions include a 50% plus one share minimum acceptance and regulatory approvals; closing is expected in mid-2027.
Qiagen also released preliminary Q3 numbers and suspended its 2026 outlook.

facts.text: Pope Leo XIV needs no further treatment after last week's surgery to remove a cancerous growth from his lung, his doctors say.
Chrome will now ask for your approval before connecting to any plain HTTP site.
GitHub says it has moved 99.99999% of its Git repositories to Azure, with a new write path for the last, busiest repos.
Sarah Guo: CVEs went from about 4,000 a month to about 15,000 since April.

facts.text: Claude API version 2026-10-21 is out, the first official version since 2023; Anthropic plans more frequent versions, and 2023-06-01 isn't deprecated.
VS Code 1.143 makes the Copilot SDK-based harness the default for new sessions and adds model comparisons.
Bun merged fixes for 7 regressions since 1.4.3 in bun install, bunx, bun patch and bun pm pack.
musl libc: CVE-2026-107891, integer overflows in regcomp that can lead to out-of-bounds writes.
Google published a Rust style guide.
